### Initialize project and install dependencies

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/ali-function-compute.md

```sh
mkdir my-app
cd my-app
npm i hono hono-alibaba-cloud-fc3-adapter
npm i -D @serverless-devs/s esbuild
mkdir src
touch src/index.ts
```

```sh
mkdir my-app
cd my-app
yarn add hono hono-alibaba-cloud-fc3-adapter
yarn add -D @serverless-devs/s esbuild
mkdir src
touch src/index.ts
```

mkdir my-app
cd my-app
pnpm add hono hono-alibaba-cloud-fc3-adapter
pnpm add -D @serverless-devs/s esbuild
mkdir src
touch src/index.ts
```

```sh
mkdir my-app

mkdir src
touch src/index.ts

### Define sample GET and POST routes

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/guides/testing.md

Defines example GET and POST endpoints on a Hono application to validate in test suites.

```ts
app.get('/posts', (c) => {
  return c.text('Many posts')
})

app.post('/posts', (c) => {
  return c.json(
    {
      message: 'Created',
    },
    201,
    {
      'X-Custom': 'Thank you',
    }
  )
})
```

### Initialize WebAssembly Hono project and install dependencies

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/webassembly-wasi.md

Initializes a new project directory and installs Hono alongside Bytecode Alliance WASI tools and Rolldown. Ensure that `type` is set to `"module"` in `package.json`.

```sh
mkdir my-app
cd my-app
npm init
npm i hono
npm i -D @bytecodealliance/jco @bytecodealliance/componentize-js @bytecodealliance/jco-std
npm i -D rolldown
```

```sh
mkdir my-app
cd my-app
npm init
yarn add hono
yarn add -D @bytecodealliance/jco @bytecodealliance/componentize-js @bytecodealliance/jco-std
yarn add -D rolldown
```

```sh
mkdir my-app
cd my-app
pnpm init --init-type module
pnpm add hono
pnpm add -D @bytecodealliance/jco @bytecodealliance/componentize-js @bytecodealliance/jco-std
pnpm add -D rolldown
```

```sh
mkdir my-app
cd my-app
npm init
bun add hono
bun add -D @bytecodealliance/jco @bytecodealliance/componentize-js @bytecodealliance/jco-std
```

### Create a basic Hono server in main.ts

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/deno.md

Define a root route handler returning text and start the HTTP server using Deno.serve with app.fetch.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'

const app = new Hono()

app.get('/', (c) => c.text('Hello Deno!'))

Deno.serve(app.fetch)
```

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/basic.md

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'

const app = new Hono()

app.get('/', (c) => {
  return c.text('Hello Hono!')
})

export default app
```

### Create a Hello World application in src/index.ts

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/nodejs.md

Set up a basic Hono web server using the serve function from @hono/node-server.

```ts
import { serve } from '@hono/node-server'
import { Hono } from 'hono'

const app = new Hono()
app.get('/', (c) => c.text('Hello Node.js!'))

serve(app)
```

--------------------------------

### Create a Hello World application with fire()

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/fastly.md

Defines a basic Fastly Compute entry point in src/index.ts using fire from @fastly/hono-fastly-compute. Use Hono from 'hono' rather than 'hono/quick' because fire builds router data during initialization.

```ts
// src/index.ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { fire } from '@fastly/hono-fastly-compute'

const app = new Hono()

app.get('/', (c) => c.text('Hello Fastly!'))

fire(app)
```

--------------------------------

### Serve static files with @hono/bun serveStatic

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/bun.md

Install the @hono/bun package and configure serveStatic middleware routes matching your file tree structure.

```sh
bun add @hono/bun
```

```ts
import { serveStatic } from '@hono/bun'

const app = new Hono()

app.use('/static/*', serveStatic({ root: './' }))
app.use('/favicon.ico', serveStatic({ path: './favicon.ico' }))
app.get('/', (c) => c.text('You can access: /static/hello.txt'))
app.get('*', serveStatic({ path: './static/fallback.txt' }))
```

```txt
./
├── favicon.ico
├── src
└── static
    ├── demo
    │   └── index.html
    ├── fallback.txt
    ├── hello.txt
    └── images
        └── dinotocat.png
```

--------------------------------

### Testing Hono application with Deno.test and @std/assert

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/deno.md

Install @std/assert, define a test file in hello.ts using app.request(), and run tests using the Deno CLI.

```sh
deno add jsr:@std/assert
```

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { assertEquals } from '@std/assert'

Deno.test('Hello World', async () => {
  const app = new Hono()
  app.get('/', (c) => c.text('Please test me'))

  const res = await app.request('http://localhost/')
  assertEquals(res.status, 200)
})
```

```sh
deno test hello.ts
```

--------------------------------

### Serve Supabase Edge Functions locally

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/supabase-functions.md

Starts the local Supabase stack and runs the Functions watcher with the `--no-verify-jwt` flag to bypass JWT verification during local development.

```bash
supabase start # start the supabase stack
supabase functions serve --no-verify-jwt # start the Functions watcher
```

### Redirect GET requests with trimTrailingSlash

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/middleware/builtin/trailing-slash.md

Trims trailing slashes from URLs on GET requests when the response status is 404.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { trimTrailingSlash } from 'hono/trailing-slash'

const app = new Hono({ strict: true })

app.use(trimTrailingSlash())
app.get('/about/me', (c) => c.text('Without Trailing Slash'))
```

### Redirect GET requests with appendTrailingSlash

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/middleware/builtin/trailing-slash.md

Appends a trailing slash to URLs when a GET request returns a 404 response status.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { appendTrailingSlash } from 'hono/trailing-slash'

const app = new Hono({ strict: true })

app.use(appendTrailingSlash())
app.get('/about/me/', (c) => c.text('With Trailing Slash'))
```

--------------------------------

### Define basic routes and HTTP method handlers

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/api/routing.md

Demonstrates routing by HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, QUERY), wildcard paths, handling all methods with app.all, custom HTTP methods, and handling multiple methods or paths with app.on.

```typescript
import { Hono } from 'hono'
const app = new Hono()
// ---cut---
// HTTP Methods
app.get('/', (c) => c.text('GET /'))
app.post('/', (c) => c.text('POST /'))
app.put('/', (c) => c.text('PUT /'))
app.delete('/', (c) => c.text('DELETE /'))
app.query('/', (c) => c.text('QUERY /'))

// Wildcard
app.get('/wild/*/card', (c) => {
  return c.text('GET /wild/*/card')
})

// Any HTTP methods
app.all('/hello', (c) => c.text('Any Method /hello'))

// Custom HTTP method
app.on('PURGE', '/cache', (c) => c.text('PURGE Method /cache'))

// Multiple Method
app.on(['PUT', 'DELETE'], '/post', (c) =>
  c.text('PUT or DELETE /post')
)

// Multiple Paths
app.on('GET', ['/hello', '/ja/hello', '/en/hello'], (c) =>
  c.text('Hello')
)
```

--------------------------------

### Test GET request with app.request

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/guides/testing.md

Sends a GET request to an endpoint using app.request and asserts the response status and text body.

```ts
describe('Example', () => {
  test('GET /posts', async () => {
    const res = await app.request('/posts')
    expect(res.status).toBe(200)
    expect(await res.text()).toBe('Many posts')
  })
})
```

### Test GET endpoint with app.request using a pathname

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/api/hono.md

Performs a simulated GET request against the application by passing a URL path string to app.request.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
const app = new Hono()
declare const test: (name: string, fn: () => void) => void
declare const expect: (value: any) => any
// ---cut---
test('GET /hello is ok', async () => {
  const res = await app.request('/hello')
  expect(res.status).toBe(200)
})
```

import { Hono } from 'hono'

})

--------------------------------

### startTime(c, name)

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/middleware/builtin/timing.md

Starts a timer for measuring the duration of a specific operation.

```APIDOC
### Description
Starts a performance timer under a given metric name for the current request context.

### Signature
`startTime(c, name)`

### Parameters
- **c** (Context) - Required - The Hono request context.
- **name** (string) - Required - Name identifier for the timer.

### Example
```ts
startTime(c, 'db')
const data = await db.findMany(...)
endTime(c, 'db')
```
```

--------------------------------

### endTime(c, name)

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/middleware/builtin/timing.md

Stops a previously started timer and records the duration in the metrics.

```APIDOC
### Description
Stops an active timer identified by name and calculates the elapsed duration for the Server-Timing header.

### Signature
`endTime(c, name)`

### Parameters
- **c** (Context) - Required - The Hono request context.
- **name** (string) - Required - Name identifier for the timer that was started.

### Example
```ts
startTime(c, 'db')
const data = await db.findMany(...)
endTime(c, 'db')
```
```

### Create a Hello World handler for Netlify Edge Functions

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/netlify.md

Define a basic Hono application in `netlify/edge-functions/index.ts` exported using `@hono/netlify`'s `handle` adapter.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'jsr:@hono/hono'
import { handle } from 'jsr:@hono/netlify'

const app = new Hono()

app.get('/', (c) => {
  return c.text('Hello Hono!')
})

export default handle(app)
```

--------------------------------

### Get all matched routes with matchedRoutes()

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/helpers/route.md

Returns an array of all routes and middleware matching the current request.

```ts
app.all('/api/*', (c, next) => {
  console.log('API middleware')
  return next()
})

app.get('/api/users/:id', (c) => {
  const routes = matchedRoutes(c)
  // Returns: [
  //   { method: 'ALL', path: '/api/*', handler: [Function] },
  //   { method: 'GET', path: '/api/users/:id', handler: [Function] }
  // ]
  return c.json({ routes: routes.length })
})
```

vite build --mode client && vite build

### Return JSON response using c.json()

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/basic.md

```ts
app.get('/api/hello', (c) => {
  return c.json({
    ok: true,
    message: 'Hello Hono!',
  })
})
```

### Get current route pattern with routePath()

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/helpers/route.md

Returns the registered route path pattern for the current handler.

```ts
app.get('/posts/:id', (c) => {
  console.log(routePath(c)) // '/posts/:id'
  return c.text('Post details')
})
```

### Get basic route information

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/helpers/route.md

Access the current route pattern and all matched routes within a request handler.

```ts
const app = new Hono()

app.get('/posts/:id', (c) => {
  const currentPath = routePath(c) // '/posts/:id'
  const routes = matchedRoutes(c) // Array of matched routes

  return c.json({
    path: currentPath,
    totalRoutes: routes.length,
  })
})
```

--------------------------------

### Get request header values with c.req.header()

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/api/request.md

Retrieve specific HTTP request headers such as User-Agent using c.req.header().

```typescript
import { Hono } from 'hono'
const app = new Hono()
// ---cut---
app.get('/', (c) => {
  const userAgent = c.req.header('User-Agent')
  //      ^?
  return c.text(`Your user agent is ${userAgent}`)
})
```

--------------------------------

### Set up WebSocket with upgradeWebSocket

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/nodejs.md

Enable WebSocket support in @hono/node-server using ws and WebSocketServer with noServer set to true.

```ts
import { serve, upgradeWebSocket } from '@hono/node-server'
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { WebSocketServer } from 'ws'

const app = new Hono()

app.get(
  '/ws',
  upgradeWebSocket(() => ({
    onMessage(event, ws) {
      ws.send(event.data)
    },
  }))
)

const wss = new WebSocketServer({ noServer: true })

serve({
  fetch: app.fetch,
  websocket: { server: wss },
})
```

### Create index.html entrypoint

Source: https://github.com/honojs/website/blob/main/docs/getting-started/service-worker.md

Provide a link to trigger the Service Worker route and load the registration module main.ts.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html>
  <body>
    <a href="/sw">Hello World by Service Worker</a>
    <script type="module" src="/main.ts"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```
